title: Capacity request sizing playbook: automated sizing, approval SLOs, and staggered activation windows
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: Our current dedicated capacity intake requires heavy manual sizing and back-and-forth between Sales/CS and Infra, which increases lead time and leads to over-provisioning. Goal: Define a playbook and implement an automated sizing assist plus approval SLA (time-to-approve) and a staggered activation window to reduce provisioning lead time by 40% while keeping SLO adherence for committed throughput. Scope: intake form UX, sizing estimator (usage profile -> recommended throughput & fleet mix), approval lanes (auto-approve vs manual review), staged activation (soft-start ramp + burst runway), and guardrails tied to autoscaling policies and fleet controls. Success metrics: median approval time <= 3 business days, first-week utilization >= 65% of committed throughput (reduces wasted capacity), customer-facing SLA on throughput guarantees documented in contract templates, and <= 5% incidents attributed to mis-provisioning in first 30 days. Out of scope: full billing/contract automation (handled by Commerce), and advanced per-tenant routing logic for multitenant fleets (to be tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form produces a recommended throughput and fleet mix with rationale linkable to telemetry; 2) Requests labeled as 'low-risk' auto-route to an approval lane with a 48-hour auto-approve SLA unless overridden; 3) Staged activation: new commitments default to a 2-step activation (warmup at 30% then scale to 100% across a configurable window); 4) Console displays estimated cost delta and expected p95 latency range for chosen sizing; 5) Playbook documented with clear escalation steps and a runbook for decommit requests.
open_questions: - What exact inputs yield reliable sizing (tokens/sec distribution, average seq len, percentile concurrency)?; - Should burst runway be billed differently or taken out of committed throughput?; - What thresholds classify a request as 'low-risk' for auto-approve?; - How to expose staged activation window choices in the intake without overwhelming non-technical users?
notes: We adopted a conservative initial sizing multiplier (1.15) to account for unknown peaks; this will be relaxed after 2 weeks of telemetry. Recommended fleet mix logic picks quantized model variant when p95 latency at recommended size exceeds SLA. Cross-functional review scheduled with Sales/Legal to align contract language for staged activations.

implementation_notes: Estimator algorithm is intentionally interpretable: uses three rule-based tiers derived from fleet performance profiles plus a small ML reweighting based on historical telemetries. Autoscaling policy hooks required: set min_capacity to 30% during warmup, allow burst_capacity to be consumed for up to X minutes before preemption. Edge case: customers with very spiky traffic (short high-frequency bursts) will need custom burst contracts.
risks: 1) Misclassification of 'low-risk' could lead to SLA breaches; mitigate by conservative thresholds and human override metrics; 2) Staged activation adds complexity to billing and contract language; need legal confirmation; 3) Incorrect estimator assumptions for new model families — include first-30-day audit and rollback path.
owner_notes: Keep the initial rollout to non-enterprise pilots to validate assumptions. After two successful pilots and telemetry confirmation, expand auto-approve thresholds and bake playbook into the onboarding flow. Maintain an incident postmortem template for any provisioning-related incidents.
